M01.intro: This module gets you into PeopleOS and around it. You sign in on your organisation's sign-in page, land on a Home page that ranks what needs you, and move through the rail, the area bar, search and the Actions panel.
M01.why: Every other module starts here. If you cannot sign in securely, read Home's signals or find a screen quickly, set-up and approvals slow down and security gaps go unnoticed.
M01.who: Everyone who signs in. What appears depends on roles: as Tenant Super Admin (full control of your organisation) you see all nine rail sections and the Administration view of Home; HR, payroll and employee roles see less.
M01.where: Sign-in: /admin/login. Home: rail › Home (/admin). Account security and Preferences: avatar menu (your initials, top right). Search, Actions, New and notifications: top bar.
objectives: Sign in, recover a forgotten password and set up an authenticator app for two-factor sign-in.
Read every card of Home in the Administration view and act on governance items and decisions.
Find any screen with the rail, the area bar, Ctrl K search and the Actions panel.
depends_on: M05 Users, access and integrations: your user, roles, the Security policy and single sign-on are managed there
M02 My work and approvals: Home's decisions lead to the Approval Center and My work
M04 Masters and configuration: Open Admin Centre and What do you want to configure? lead there
M26 Signing out and staying secure: sign-out, sessions and safe handling of data

home/home.purpose: Your starting page. It greets you, sums up in one sentence what needs you today and ranks governance items, decisions and shortcuts for the view you choose.
home/home.when: Every time you sign in, and whenever you want to see what is waiting for you.
elements: Date, organisation and one sentence from real counts (example: 2 governance items need attention, 8 decisions wait).
Open Admin Centre opens All modules; Start something opens search in Actions mode, like New.
Switches Home between People operations, Administration, Payroll and Company. Your choice is remembered.
Access and security gaps, most severe first, each with its reason and a Review button to the screen that fixes it.
Tiles: configuration changes this week, active users, roles, multi-factor sign-in, audited events. Each tile opens its page.
Up to four requests waiting for you; Review opens it in a side drawer. Approval Center lists them all.
Generated statements from records you may see, each with its source and a link. It suggests; you decide.
Most badges this month (link: Recognition) and your usual admin actions; All actions shows every action.
home/home.after: Your choices are saved for you alone: View as becomes how Home opens (also in Preferences › Home opens as); Got it hides the welcome note for good.
home/home.permission: Open to every signed-in person. The Administration view needs user.assign_roles, settings.update or configuration.publish; each card needs access to the screen it opens (e.g. security.manage for the MFA item).
home/home.depends: An active organisation and user. Personal cards (For you, My day, leave) appear only when your user is linked to an employee record.
home/home.limits: Counts are worked out when the page loads; reload to refresh. The Administration view has no What changed feed. Cards for everyone are set in Setup › Access rights › Widget access.

procedures.title: Activate your account from the invitation
procedures.before: You have the e-mail 'You have been invited to <organisation> on PeopleOS'. Its link works once and the e-mail states when it expires (UTC).
steps: Click Accept the invitation in the e-mail. The page Accept your invitation says: Choose a password for <your e-mail>.
Type it in Password and again in Confirm password, following your organisation's password rules. The eye icon shows what you typed.
Click Activate my account. You see 'Your account is ready. Sign in with your new password.' and the sign-in page opens.
Enter your work e-mail and new password and click Sign in. If two-factor sign-in is required, set up your authenticator first.
procedures.result: Your account is active and your e-mail address is confirmed. This browser now remembers your organisation for the sign-in page.

procedures.title: Sign in
procedures.before: Your account is active. Use your work e-mail address.
steps: Go to /admin/login (/login also leads there). A browser that has signed in before shows 'Sign in to <your organisation>' with your logo.
Fill Email address and Password (both required). The eye icon in the Password box shows the password.
Remember me only on your own device
Tick Remember me only on a device that nobody else uses: it keeps this browser signed in until you sign out.
Click Sign in. If you use an authenticator, the page asks Verify your identity: enter the 6-digit code and click Confirm sign in.
Home opens in your chosen view. If a link sent you to sign in, you go back to the page that link pointed to.
procedures.result: You are signed in. Sign-ins and failed attempts are recorded in the audit trail (Insights › Audit › Change history).
procedures.source: app/Filament/Auth/Login.php; resources/views/filament/auth/login.blade.php; vendor Filament Auth/Pages/Login.php (fields, 5 attempts a minute); app/Domain/Audit/Listeners/RecordAuthenticationEvents.php

procedures.title: Reset a forgotten password
procedures.before: Your account is active. A person who has not yet activated an invitation must use the invitation instead.
steps: On the sign-in page click Forgot password? beside Password.
Enter your Email address and click Send email. The answer is always the same, so it never reveals whether an address has an account.
Subject 'Reset your PeopleOS password'. Click Choose a new password. The link works once and expires after the minutes stated (60 as set).
On Reset your password, your e-mail is filled in. Enter Password and Confirm password under your organisation's rules; click Reset password.
You see 'Your password has been changed. Sign in with it now.' Every other session of yours has been signed out.
procedures.result: A new password is set and all old sessions are ended. Two-factor sign-in is unchanged: you still need your authenticator.

procedures.title: Set up two-factor sign-in (authenticator app)
procedures.before: Install an authenticator app on your phone, for example Google Authenticator.
steps: Click your initials (top right) › Account security.
Under Two-factor authentication (2FA), next to Authenticator app, click Set up.
Scan the QR code with the app, or type the code shown under 'Or enter this code manually'.
Enter the 6-digit code from the app and your Current password, then continue.
Copy or download the recovery codes and store them offline. They are shown once; each works once if you lose the phone.
Click Enable authenticator app. Authenticator app now reads Enabled, with Regenerate recovery codes and Turn off.
procedures.result: From the next sign-in PeopleOS asks for a 6-digit code after your password, also when a remembered browser opens a new session.
procedures.source: app/Filament/Auth/EditProfile.php; AdminPanelProvider (AppAuthentication recoverable); app/Domain/Identity/Services/MultiFactor.php; Filament MFA set-up action

procedures.title: Sign in with a recovery code (phone lost)
procedures.before: You have your saved recovery codes.
steps: Enter Email address and Password and click Sign in. The page asks Verify your identity.
Click Use a recovery code instead, enter one code in Or, enter a recovery code and click Confirm sign in.
Open Account security. Turn off the old authenticator and Set up the new phone, or Regenerate recovery codes.
procedures.result: You are back in with a new authenticator. The used recovery code no longer works; the change is recorded in the audit trail.

procedures.title: Change your own password
steps: Fill New password and Confirm new password. Current password appears once you type; fill it too.
Click Save changes. A rule you miss is named under the field, e.g. 'Include a number.'
procedures.result: The new password applies at once; your other open sessions on other devices are signed out at their next click.

procedures.title: Start your day from Home
procedures.before: You are signed in; Home opens in the Administration view (or the view you chose).
steps: The sentence under the greeting counts governance items and decisions waiting for you. 'You're all caught up' means nothing needs you.
Read each item's reason and click Review. In the example, 'Multi-factor sign-in is not required' opens the Security policy.
Click a tile to open its list: Active users and Roles open Users and Roles; Audited events this week opens Change history.
In Decisions waiting for you click Review: the request opens in a side drawer. 'n more in the Approval Center' lists the rest.
Use the shortcuts on the right (Invite a user, What do you want to configure?, All modules, Manage roles and permissions) or All actions.
procedures.result: Governance gaps and waiting decisions are handled or knowingly left; Home's counts fall when you reload it.
procedures.source: app/Filament/Pages/Home.php; resources/views/filament/pages/home.blade.php and home/*.blade.php; app/Domain/Experience/Services/HomeComposer.php, RoleLens.php, RoleSignals.php (governance), QuickActions.php, ContextualIntelligence.php

procedures.title: Change the Home view and how Home opens
procedures.before: You hold more than one kind of work (for an administrator: People operations, Administration, Payroll, Company).
steps: In the hero's View as row click a chip, e.g. Payroll: Home shows the latest pay run, its stage and exceptions.
Your last chip is remembered. Or open avatar menu › Preferences › Home opens as and pick a view, or Automatic.
Preferences › Home and history › Restore hidden Home cards brings back cards you hid.
procedures.result: Home, the rail's preferred landings, search result order and the phone bar follow your chosen view. Access never changes with the view.

procedures.title: Open a screen with the rail and area bar
steps: In the rail click a section, e.g. People. Its areas unfold under it (its plus turns to a minus); any other open section folds.
Click an area, e.g. Lifecycle. It opens on its desk (Lifecycle desk) or its main page.
The bar above the page reads 'People / Lifecycle' and lists the page you are on first, then favourites, the desk and everyday pages.
Click the star beside the current page's name. Starred pages stay at the front of the bar and in a Favourites row.
Click All in … (the area name) (with its count) to list every page grouped by purpose; type in Find in the area to narrow it.
procedures.result: You reach any page in two or three clicks and keep your everyday pages one click away.

procedures.title: Find anything with Ctrl K
steps: Click the top-bar box 'Search people, requests, actions…', or press Ctrl K (⌘K on a Mac) or /.
Type a name, request number, policy word or what you want to do, e.g. 'leave'. Results are grouped: Intelligence, Actions, Navigation, People and more.
Click Everything, Actions or People (or press Tab) to search only that.
Move with the arrow keys and press Enter to open; Ctrl+Enter previews; the right arrow shows a result's actions; Esc closes.
procedures.result: The page, person or form opens. Items you open are kept as Recent, at the top of search and in the rail.

procedures.title: Run an HR action from the Actions panel
procedures.before: Your roles allow at least one HR action (the button shows only then).
steps: Click Actions in the top bar. A full-screen panel lists actions by module: Workforce, Time office, Payroll, Expense & travel, and more.
Type in Search actions… to filter as you type, or scan a module's list.
Click the pin beside an action. Pinned and Recent actions appear as chips at the top of the panel.
Click the action. Its screen, or the form on that screen, opens; the module's own checks and approvals apply.
procedures.result: The action's form is open in its module. Esc or the close button leaves the panel.

procedures.title: Read and clear notifications
steps: Click the bell in the top bar; its number is your unread notifications (25 in the example). A Notifications panel slides in.
Open a notification's link, or use Mark all as read and Clear.
For tabs (All, Needs attention, Approvals, Mentions, Announcements, Updates, System) open My work › Notifications.
procedures.result: Unread items are handled. The bell refreshes on its own about every 30 seconds.

procedures.title: Work with a list page
procedures.before: Open a list, e.g. People › Lifecycle › Employees.
steps: Type in the search box; click the funnel (its badge counts active filters), set filters and apply them.
Views › Save this view… keeps filters, search, sort and columns under a name for you only; tick 'Open this register with this view' for a default.
Click a column heading to sort; the columns icon at the right of the toolbar shows or hides columns.
At the bottom: 'Showing 1 to 10 of 23 results', Per page and page numbers.
Use the row's View or Edit. Forms run as steps and end with a review of your changes before you save.
procedures.result: You see exactly the records you need; your saved view returns next time.

calculations.title: Decisions waiting for you on Home
calculations.intro: Home lists at most four decisions and links to the rest in the Approval Center. Figures are from the example organisation.
lines: More in the Approval Center (link '4 more in the Approval Center')
explain: Home takes the first four pending items; the link shows the count minus four. A '+' means more wait than the queue could count.
The brief, the card heading count and the My work badge in the rail.

calculations.title: When a password expires and when the reminder comes
calculations.intro: Illustrative: the example organisation has expiry off (Expire after days = 0). With 90 days and a 7-day reminder:
explain: Expiry date = date of last change + Expire after days. The reminder (in-app and e-mail) comes once, from 7 days before: 25 Mar 2026.
At the next sign-in or click after expiry, the person must choose a new password. Single sign-on sessions are not affected.

warnings.title: Set up your own authenticator before requiring it
warnings.headline: Requiring two-factor sign-in affects everyone at their next click, you included.
warnings.body: When 'Require authenticator-app MFA for every tenant login' is on, anyone without an authenticator is sent to Set up two-factor authentication before anything else.
points: Set up yours in Account security first.
Tell people to install an authenticator app beforehand.
Only the authenticator app method is offered.
warnings.todo: Turn the rule on in Admin › Platform › Security policy (see M05).

warnings.title: Keep your recovery codes
warnings.headline: You cannot reset your own authenticator.
warnings.body: Recovery codes are shown once. Without your phone and codes, another administrator with security.manage must use Reset multi-factor authentication on your user.
points: Store the codes offline, not on the phone.
Make sure a second administrator exists.
If you are the only administrator, ask PeopleOS support.
warnings.todo: Download or copy the codes during set-up; regenerate them if you think they were seen.

warnings.title: Multi-factor sign-in is not required
warnings.headline: The example organisation's Home shows this governance item.
warnings.body: Anyone with a password can sign in. A leaked password is then enough to reach salaries and personal data.
points: The At a glance tile reads Optional while it is off.
Review opens the Security policy.
warnings.todo: Turn on two-factor sign-in once your people have authenticators.

warnings.title: Sign-in pauses, not account locks
warnings.headline: After five failed attempts in a minute from one network, the form pauses.
warnings.body: You see 'Too many login attempts' with the seconds to wait. There is no permanent lock on the account; a wrong password and an inactive account show the same message on purpose.
points: Wait the seconds shown.
Use Forgot password? if unsure.
Failed attempts are recorded in the audit trail.

warnings.title: Single sign-on has no button on the sign-in page
warnings.headline: People who sign in through your identity provider need its Login URL.
warnings.body: The sign-in page offers e-mail and password only. Each single sign-on connection has its own Login URL (/sso/<slug>/redirect).
points: Copy the Login URL from Admin › Platform › Single sign-on (M05).
Share it in your welcome e-mail.

troubleshooting: 'These credentials do not match our records.'
Wrong e-mail or password, or the account cannot sign in (invited, suspended, organisation suspended). The message is the same on purpose.
Check the address and Caps Lock; use Forgot password?; ask another administrator to check your user in Admin › Setup › Users.
'Too many login attempts. Please try again in N seconds.'
Five attempts in a minute from this network address.
Wait the seconds shown, then try once, or reset the password.
'This invitation link is invalid or has expired…'
The link was used, replaced by a newer invitation or has expired.
For your own account ask PeopleOS support; for your people use Send a new invitation on the user's Account menu.
'This password reset link is invalid or has expired. Request a new one.'
The link is older than 60 minutes, was used, or a newer one was requested.
Request a new link and use only the newest e-mail.
The page 'Choose a new password' after signing in
Your password is older than the organisation's Expire after days.
Enter Current password, a new one twice and click Change password.
The page 'Set up two-factor authentication'
Your organisation requires two-factor sign-in and you have no authenticator.
Set up the authenticator app, keep the recovery codes, then Continue.
The page 'Confirm it is you'
A remembered or single sign-on session must still prove your authenticator.
Enter a code or a recovery code and click Verify, or Sign out.
'Your network is not allowed to access this tenant.'
The Security policy's IP allowlist does not include your network.
Use an allowed network or ask an administrator to add yours; if nobody can reach PeopleOS, ask PeopleOS support.
A section or page is missing from the rail
Sections and pages appear only when your roles let you open them.
Check your roles in Admin › Setup › Users (M05).
Another organisation's logo on the sign-in page
The browser remembers the last organisation that signed in on it.
Click 'Not <name>? Use another organisation' under the form.
checklist: Activate your account
Accept the invitation before it expires and choose a strong password.
Set up your authenticator
Account security › Set up; keep the recovery codes offline.
Clear Home's Governance card
Review each item, fix it or confirm it is intended.
Choose how Home opens
View as, or Preferences › Home opens as.
Star your everyday pages
Use the area bar star so they stay first.
Learn the shortcuts
Press ? for the list; Ctrl K searches; N starts something new.
Share your sign-in link
Admin › Setup › Setup (Core HR) › Sign-in link, for welcome e-mails.
summary: Sign in at /admin/login with your work e-mail; once a browser has signed in, the page shows your organisation.
Password rules, expiry, reuse and two-factor sign-in are checked on every page, not only at sign-in.
Home's Administration view shows governance gaps, key counts and decisions waiting, each with Review.
The rail has nine sections; the area bar shows an area's pages, your starred favourites and All in ….
Ctrl K finds people, pages and actions; Actions lists every HR action by module; New starts something.
You only ever see what your roles allow: navigation and views never grant access.

gaps: Sign-in, forgot/reset password, invitation, two-factor, expired-password, Account security and Preferences pages are not in the crawl; described from source code only.
There is no separate Help menu in the workspace; help comes from page subheadings, the ? shortcuts list, Ask PeopleOS and Knowledge articles.
Remember me duration and the server session lifetime are service settings not visible to the organisation (framework default for Remember me is about 400 days); confirm with PeopleOS support.
When an idle timeout or an ended session signs a person out, the sign-in page does not show the reason (the message is stored but not displayed).
The number of actions in the Actions panel for this role and the rail's Pinned people / Recent lists were not captured.
The rail's Recent list fills only from items opened through Ctrl K search, not from every page visited.
Approvals (Approval Center, /admin/approvals) is not listed in the rail for this role; it is reached from Home, G then A, or the phone bar.

auth/login.purpose: The sign-in page. Your form is on the right; the left shows your organisation's picture or logo once this browser has signed in to it, otherwise the PeopleOS artwork.
auth/login.when: Each time you start working, or when a session has ended.
elements: Heading; reads 'Sign in to PeopleOS' in a browser that remembers no organisation.
Link beside Password to the password reset request.
Shows or hides the password you typed.
Makes this browser forget your organisation and show the PeopleOS page.

fields.label: Remember me
fields.meaning: Keeps this browser signed in until you sign out. Only on your own device.

auth/login.after: With an authenticator the same page asks for a 6-digit code (Verify your identity › Confirm sign in); then Home opens.
auth/login.depends: An active user in an active organisation.
auth/login.limits: No single sign-on button; no permanent account lock, only a short pause after five attempts a minute.
auth/login.source: app/Filament/Auth/Login.php; resources/views/filament/auth/login.blade.php; vendor Filament Auth/Pages/Login.php (fields, 5 attempts a minute); app/Filament/Support/SignInBranding.php; app/Domain/Identity/Services/RememberedWorkspace.php

auth/forgot-password.purpose: Asks PeopleOS to e-mail a one-time link to choose a new password.
auth/forgot-password.when: When you have forgotten your password.
elements: Sends the link if the address belongs to an active account; the answer is the same either way.

fields.label: Email address
fields.meaning: The address you sign in with.

auth/forgot-password.after: Notice: 'If an account uses that address, we have sent it a link to choose a new password.' The link expires in 60 minutes.
auth/forgot-password.depends: An active account. Invited people use their invitation instead.
auth/forgot-password.limits: Two requests a minute from one network; each address is also limited.

auth/reset-password.purpose: Choose a new password from the e-mailed link.
elements: Saves the new password if the link is valid.

fields.label: Password
fields.meaning: New password under your organisation's rules.

auth/reset-password.after: All your sessions end; sign in with the new password. Two-factor sign-in stays as it was.
auth/reset-password.depends: A link less than 60 minutes old, not yet used.
auth/reset-password.limits: Any problem with the link shows one message: 'This password reset link is invalid or has expired. Request a new one.'

auth/accept-invitation.purpose: Activates an invited account: the invitee chooses a password, then signs in.
auth/accept-invitation.when: First access of an invited account (for you, the e-mail from PeopleOS).
elements: Saves the password and activates the account.

fields.label: Password
fields.meaning: Your new password under the organisation's rules.

auth/accept-invitation.after: 'Your account is ready. Sign in with your new password.' and the sign-in page opens.
auth/accept-invitation.depends: A pending invitation; you must be signed out.
auth/accept-invitation.limits: Works once; expires at the time stated in the e-mail.

auth/choose-password.purpose: Shown before anything else when a password has expired ('Choose a new password') or after signing in with a temporary password ('Choose your own password').
auth/choose-password.when: At the first click after expiry, or at the first sign-in with a temporary password.
elements: Saves the new password and continues to the page you wanted.

fields.label: Current password / Temporary password
fields.meaning: The password you signed in with.

fields.label: New password
fields.meaning: Must differ from the current one and meet the rules.

auth/choose-password.after: 'Your password has been changed.' Your other sessions are signed out; this one continues.
auth/choose-password.depends: Expiry set in Security policy, or a temporary password from an administrator.
auth/choose-password.limits: Single sign-on sessions are never sent here.

auth/confirm-it-is-you.purpose: Asks for your authenticator code when a session started without the code step (Remember me or single sign-on).
auth/confirm-it-is-you.when: When a remembered browser or single sign-on opens a new session and you have an authenticator.
elements: Switches to a one-time recovery code.

fields.label: Enter the 6-digit code from the authenticator app
fields.meaning: The current code in your app.

auth/confirm-it-is-you.after: You continue to the page you asked for.
auth/confirm-it-is-you.depends: An authenticator set up on your account.

M26.intro: Signing out ends your session in this browser. This module explains what sign-out ends and what it does not, how to use shared devices safely, how to look after your password and authenticator, and how to handle payroll and employee data.
M26.why: An organisation administrator can see and change everything. A session left open or a weak password exposes the salaries, bank details and identity data of every employee.
M26.who: Everyone signs out the same way. The organisation-wide controls (Security policy, Sign out everywhere, Reset multi-factor authentication) need security.manage or the right to update users; Tenant Super Admin holds both.
M26.where: Avatar menu (your initials, top right) › Sign out. Avatar menu › Account security. Admin › Platform › Security policy. Admin › Setup › Users › a user › Account.
objectives: Sign out correctly and know what stays signed in elsewhere.
Protect your account with a strong password, an authenticator and recovery codes.
Run a regular security routine for your organisation.

procedures.title: Sign out
procedures.before: Save your work: a form with unsaved changes asks before you leave it.
steps: Click your initials at the top right of any page.
Click Sign out, the last item in the menu.
The sign-in page opens. On a shared device, close every browser window too.
procedures.result: This browser's session is over and Remember me no longer works on any device. The sign-out is recorded in the audit trail.
procedures.source: Filament user menu (logout) and LogoutController; Laravel SessionGuard::logout; app/Domain/Audit/Listeners/RecordAuthenticationEvents.php

procedures.title: Leave a shared computer safely
procedures.before: You signed in on a computer other people use.
steps: Leave Remember me empty, and do not let the browser save your password.
Delete payslips, reports, bank files and exports you saved; PeopleOS cannot protect files on the computer.
On the sign-in page click 'Not <organisation>? Use another organisation' so the page no longer shows your logo.
procedures.result: Nothing of your session, password or downloaded data is left on the device.

procedures.title: End your sessions on other devices
procedures.before: You think you left PeopleOS open elsewhere, or your password may be known.
steps: Fill New password, Confirm new password and Current password, then Save changes.
If your recovery codes may have been seen, click Regenerate recovery codes.
procedures.result: Every other session of yours is signed out at its next click; this one continues.

procedures.title: Sign a person out everywhere or reset their authenticator
procedures.before: A device is lost or stolen, or a person must lose access at once. You cannot do this for your own account.
steps: Admin › Setup › Users, then Edit on the person's row.
Click the Account button at the top of the page.
Click Sign out everywhere, give a Reason (5 characters or more) and confirm: 'Signed out on every device.'
Click Reset multi-factor authentication (needs security.manage) with a reason; they set up a new authenticator at their next sign-in.
Click E-mail a temporary password: the old password stops working and they choose their own at sign-in.
procedures.result: The person's sessions end on every device; the action and your reason are in the audit trail.

procedures.title: Set automatic sign-out and access rules
steps: Admin › Platform › Security policy. The form runs in steps: Access, Passwords, Disable login, Retention, Data warehouse feed, Review.
Set Sign out after idle minutes (0 = never), Require authenticator-app MFA for every tenant login and, if needed, the IP allowlist.
Minimum length, Expire after days, Remind before expiry (days), Recently used passwords that cannot be reused and the two Strict password options.
Go to Review and click Save policy: 'Security policy saved'.
procedures.result: The rules apply at everyone's next click. Details of every field are in M05.

calculations.title: When the idle timeout signs someone out
calculations.intro: Illustrative: the example organisation has Sign out after idle minutes = 0 (never). With 30 minutes:
total: First click after this time signs the person out
explain: On each click PeopleOS compares the time since the previous click with the setting; more than the setting ends the session.
The sign-in page, without a message. Unsaved form entries are lost.

warnings.title: The IP allowlist can lock you out
warnings.headline: The allowlist applies to everyone in your organisation, you included.
warnings.body: From a network that is not listed, every page answers 'Your network is not allowed to access this tenant.' Only PeopleOS platform staff are exempt.
points: Add your own office and VPN addresses first.
Use exact IPs, 10.0.* style or CIDR (10.0.0.0/8).
Leave it empty for no restriction.
warnings.todo: If no administrator can reach PeopleOS after a change, ask PeopleOS support.

warnings.title: Signing out here does not sign you out elsewhere
warnings.headline: Open sessions on other devices continue.
warnings.body: Sign-out ends this browser's session and stops Remember me everywhere, but a browser that is already signed in elsewhere stays in until it times out.
points: Change your password to end them all.
An administrator can use Sign out everywhere on another person.

warnings.title: Downloaded files leave PeopleOS's protection
warnings.headline: Access rules stop at the download.
warnings.body: Payslips, reports, bank files and data exports saved to a computer are readable by anyone with that computer.
points: Download only what you need.
Store files in your organisation's secure storage.
Delete local copies after use.

warnings.title: Never share an account
warnings.headline: Every change is recorded under the person who signed in.
warnings.body: The audit trail names who did what. PeopleOS never shows anyone's password; a generated temporary password is shown once, to hand over.
points: Give each person their own user and role.
Do not ask for or send passwords by e-mail or chat.

troubleshooting: Back on the sign-in page while working, with no message
Idle timeout, your password changed elsewhere, Sign out everywhere or an authenticator reset by an administrator, or the account was suspended.
Sign in again. If you did not expect it, change your password and tell another administrator.
Signed out after a short break
Sign out after idle minutes is set in Security policy.
Sign in again; save forms before you step away.
The sign-in page still shows your logo after sign-out
By design: the browser remembers your organisation's look; this grants nothing.
Click 'Not <name>? Use another organisation' to make the browser forget it.
'Enter your password' before My payslips or My compensation
Setup › Payroll: 'Ask for the password again before My compensation, My payslips and My salary YTD' is on.
Enter your sign-in password; it is not asked again for 15 minutes.
You cannot see Sign out everywhere for yourself
The action is offered only for other people's users.
Change your own password in Account security instead.
checklist: Every day: sign out
Avatar menu › Sign out when you stop; close the browser on shared devices.
Every day: read Governance on Home
Act on MFA, role and scope gaps and on failures it lists.
Every day: no Remember me on shared devices
Tick it only on a device that only you use.
Every week: check Change history
Insights › Audit › Change history: filter Action by Login Failed, Login and Mfa Changed.
Every week: delete local downloads
Payslips, reports, bank files and exports after use.
Every month: review Users
Leavers inactive, everyone with a role, approvers scoped to their organisation.
Keep two-factor sign-in required
Security policy › Require authenticator-app MFA for every tenant login.
Set an idle timeout
Security policy › Sign out after idle minutes: choose a value that suits your organisation.
Keep a second administrator
Someone with security.manage who can reset your authenticator.
Keep recovery codes offline
Regenerate them if they may have been seen.
Control the assistant's data
Setup › Governance › Data the assistant may send to an external AI provider.
summary: Sign out from the avatar menu; it ends this browser's session and Remember me on every device.
Other open sessions stay in until they time out; change your password to end them all.
Use Remember me only on your own device; on shared ones sign out, delete downloads and close the browser.
Keep two-factor sign-in on, recovery codes offline and a second administrator who can reset you.
Treat payslips, reports and exports as confidential: once downloaded, PeopleOS cannot protect them.
